subject.title: Synchronous crypto.createHash blocks Node.js event loop on large MCP schemas

question: Should this issue be treated as enough proof to queue a bundle-MCP config-hash performance fix, or should maintainers ask for a focused reproduction that distinguishes large launch config from large returned tool schemas?
rationale: Source proves synchronous hashing exists, but the reported schema example does not feed the cited line and the best fix changes if the real blocker is config serialization versus tool-catalog schema handling.

options.title: Ask For Focused Reproduction
options.body: Request a small repro or benchmark that shows whether large `mcp.servers` launch config or returned `inputSchema` payloads block Gateway heartbeats before queueing repair.

options.title: Queue Config-Hash Repair
options.body: Treat the synchronous config-hash source evidence as sufficient and ask for a bounded nonblocking fingerprint helper with regression coverage.

options.title: Split Schema Catalog Follow-Up
options.body: Keep this issue scoped to CLI launch-config hashing and open or link a separate issue if returned-schema catalog blocking is reproduced.

recommendation.title: Ask For Focused Reproduction
recommendation.body: Request a small repro or benchmark that shows whether large `mcp.servers` launch config or returned `inputSchema` payloads block Gateway heartbeats before queueing repair.

likelyOwner.reason: vincentkoc has recent history across both MCP runtime and bundle-MCP surfaces involved in distinguishing the source paths.
